item.title: Building a Home Datacenter with a Raspberry Pi Cluster - 2. Initial Cluster Setup
item.description:
Note: I’m based in Korea, so some context here is Korea-specific.

Hardware

Set up your hardware as shown in the diagram above.

If you already use a computer at home, you most likely already have a router and a desktop set up, so you only need to add the parts marked in green.

If you bought an unmanaged switch hub online, just plug all of the Raspberry Pi LAN cables into the switch hub, then run a single internet cable from your router to the switch.

item.title: Building a Datacenter at Home with a Raspberry Pi Cluster - Introduction
item.description:
Note: I’m based in Korea, so some context here is Korea-specific.

About 300 days have passed since I first built my Raspberry Pi cluster.

The trigger wasn’t really that big a deal.

Every morning on my way to work, I read a news curation service called GeekNews 1, and one day an article titled Chick-Fil-A’s Edge Computing Architecture: Enterprise Restaurant Compute caught my eye.

After that, the thought of “even Chick-Fil-A runs Kubernetes, so as a server engineer, shouldn’t I have at least one cluster of my own to manage?” was where it all began.
